fullPassage: Reformist approaches assume that markets could operate in more equitable and environmentally reasonable ways, and that a market is the most efficient option available. Yet the logic of market efficiencies generally rotates on purely monetary calculations, effectively reasoning in a hall of mirrors and marginalising real social and environmental values. Familiar examples are conventional food retailers, such as supermarkets, which purchase fruit and vegetables as cheaply as possible. Inexpensive produce might be grown using soil- and water-damaging fertilisers, by poorly paid illegal migrant workers, and transported long distances using more cheap labour and environmentally damaging practices. However, organic farmers can only follow ecologically sound practices and make sure they pay their workers fair wages if the food costs more, meaning supply for an elite demand. By its very nature, one never manages to escape the conundrums that production for trade entails. Real social and environmental values involved in caring for people and Earth highlighting the inequities and damage of market-oriented activities.

questions.passage: Reformist approaches assume that markets could operate in more (A)[equitable / inequitable] and environmentally reasonable ways, and that a market is the most (B)[efficient / inefficient] option available. Yet the logic of market efficiencies generally rotates on purely (C)[monetary / emotional] calculations, effectively reasoning in a hall of mirrors and marginalising real social and environmental values.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 더 공정한(equitable) 방식. 가장 효율적인(efficient) 선택지. 순전히 금전적(monetary) 계산.
det.analysis:
✅ ① equitable — efficient — monetary: 원문 일치
❌ ② inequitable(불공정한): equitable(공정한)이 원문
❌ ③ inefficient(비효율적인): efficient(효율적인)이 원문
❌ ④ emotional(감정적인): monetary(금전적인)이 원문
det.tip: equitable(공정한) ↔ inequitable(불공정한), efficient(효율적인) ↔ inefficient(비효율적인), monetary(금전적인) ↔ emotional(감정적인)

questions.passage: Familiar examples are (A)[conventional / unconventional] food retailers, such as supermarkets, which purchase fruit and vegetables as cheaply as possible. det.korean: 기존의(conventional) 식품 소매업체. 저렴한(inexpensive) 농산물. 환경적으로 해로운(damaging) 관행.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ conventional — Inexpensive — damaging: 원문 일치
❌ ① unconventional(비관행적인): conventional(기존의)이 원문
❌ ② Expensive(비싼): Inexpensive(저렴한)가 원문
❌ ④ beneficial(유익한): damaging(해로운)이 원문
det.tip: conventional(기존의) ↔ unconventional(비관행적인), inexpensive(저렴한) ↔ expensive(비싼), damaging(해로운) ↔ beneficial(유익한)

questions.passage: However, organic farmers can only follow (A)[ecologically / economically] sound practices and make sure they pay their workers fair wages if the food costs more, meaning supply for an (B)[elite / universal] demand. det.analysis:
✅ ④ ecologically — elite — escape: 원문 일치
❌ ① economically(경제적으로): ecologically(생태적으로)가 원문
❌ ② universal(보편적인): elite(엘리트)가 원문
❌ ③ embrace(받아들이다): escape(벗어나다)가 원문
det.tip: ecologically(생태적으로) ↔ economically(경제적으로), elite(엘리트) ↔ universal(보편적인), escape(벗어나다) ↔ embrace(받아들이다)

questions.passage: Reformist approaches assume that markets could operate in more equitable and environmentally reasonable ways, and that a market is the most efficient option available. Yet the logic of market efficiencies generally rotates on purely monetary calculations, effectively reasoning in a hall of mirrors and marginalising real social and environmental values. Familiar examples are conventional food retailers, such as supermarkets, which purchase fruit and vegetables as <u>① cheaply</u> as possible. Inexpensive produce might be grown using soil- and water-damaging fertilisers, by poorly paid illegal migrant workers, and <u>② transported</u> long distances using more cheap labour and environmentally damaging practices. However, organic farmers can only follow ecologically sound practices and make sure they pay their workers <u>③ fair</u> wages if the food costs more, meaning supply for an elite demand. By its very nature, one never manages to escape the conundrums that production for trade <u>④ avoids</u>.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중에서 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.analysis:
✅ ① cheaply: 저렴하게, 원문 일치
✅ ② transported: 운송된, 원문 일치
✅ ③ fair: 공정한, 원문 일치
❌ ④ avoids(피하다) → entails(수반하다): 반의어적 관계. 무역 생산이 난제를 '수반한다'는 맥락.
det.tip: entail(수반하다) ↔ avoid(피하다). production for trade entails conundrums(무역 생산은 난제를 수반한다)

questions.stem: 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중에서 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ③ 원문은 '적은 임금을 받는(poorly paid)'인데 '후하게(generously) 임금을 받는'으로 바뀌었다.

✅ ① marginalising: 주변화하다, 원문 일치
✅ ② conventional: 기존의, 원문 일치
❌ ③ generously(후하게) → poorly(적게): 반의어. 불법 이주 노동자가 '적은 임금'을 받는 맥락.
✅ ④ sound: 건전한, 원문 일치
det.tip: poorly paid(적은 임금) ↔ generously paid(후한 임금). 저렴한 농산물의 숨겨진 비용을 드러내는 맥락.
